sourceDesc.p: Traduction anglaise auto-generee (IA, non relue par un latiniste) a partir du texte latin deja present dans le corpus sous zoo3/4l (12 hymnes attribues a Ambroise, avec des degres divers d'authenticite selon la tradition manuscrite : seule une poignee sont unanimement considerees comme authentiquement ambrosiennes, les autres relevant d'une tradition hymnique plus large attribuee a l'eveque de Milan). Aucune traduction anglaise du domaine public couvrant exactement cet ensemble de 12 hymnes n'a ete trouvee (les traductions historiques disponibles, par ex. celles de J.M. Neale, sont dispersees, partielles, et souvent recomposees pour l'usage liturgique plutot que fideles vers pour vers a l'edition latine ici presente) ; une traduction fraiche a donc ete produite. Chaque strophe latine de quatre vers (tetrametre iambique) est rendue par un seul paragraphe en prose anglaise continue plutot que vers pour vers, pour privilegier la fidelite du sens sur la forme metrique. A verifier par un latiniste avant toute citation savante ; quelques passages theologiquement elliptiques (ex. l'hymne d'Epiphanie) comportent une part d'interpretation. Correspond au texte latin deja present dans le corpus sous zoo3/4l.

div.head: Hymn 1: Aeterne rerum conditor
div.p: Eternal creator of all things, who rules night and day and grants the seasons their times, that you may relieve our weariness,
already the herald of day sounds, the watchman of deepest night, a nocturnal light for travellers, separating night from night.
Roused by this, the morning star clears the sky of darkness; at this, every band of wrongdoers abandons its path of harm.
At this the sailor gathers his strength, and the straits of the sea grow calm; at this the very Rock of the Church, hearing it crow, washes away its fault.
Let us then rise briskly: the cock rouses those lying down, and rebukes the sleepy; the cock reproves those who deny.
When the cock crows, hope returns, health is restored to the sick, the robber's blade is sheathed, faith returns to the fallen.
Jesus, look upon us as we stumble, and correct us by your gaze; if you look upon us, our lapses fall away, and by weeping our guilt is dissolved.
Shine, O light, upon our senses, and shake off the sleep of the mind: let our voice sound you first, and let us pay our vows to you.

div.head: Hymn 2: Deus creator omnium
div.p: God, creator of all things, and ruler of the sky, clothing the day with becoming light, and the night with the grace of sleep,
so that rest may restore our relaxed limbs to the service of labour, relieve our weary minds, and dissolve our anxious griefs.
Now that the day is done we render thanks, and at the rising of night, prayers; with vows, that you may help us who are guilty, we pay as we sing this hymn.
Let the depths of our heart sing to you, let our tuneful voice resound to you, let chaste love cherish you, let a sober mind adore you.
So that when the deep gloom of night has shut in the day, faith may know no darkness, and night may shine bright through faith.
Do not let the mind sleep; let sin alone know how to sleep; let watchful faith, cooling temptation, temper the heat of slumber.
Freed from slippery sense, let the depths of the heart dream of you; nor let fear, through the wiles of the envious enemy, rouse us from our rest.
Let us ask Christ and the Father, and the Spirit of Christ and the Father: one power, mighty through all things, O Trinity, cherish us as we pray.

div.head: Hymn 3: Jam surgit hora tertia
div.p: Now the third hour rises, in which Christ mounted the cross; let the mind think nothing arrogant, let it direct its feeling to prayer.
He who receives Christ in his heart bears a guiltless mind, and by his earnest vows he ensures that he deserves the Holy Spirit.
This is the hour which put an end to the age-old sluggishness of dread sin, and washed away the kingdom of death, and lifted guilt away from the age.
From here the blessed times began, by the grace of Christ; truth filled the Churches throughout the whole world with faith.
From the lofty summit of his triumph he spoke to his mother: "Behold, mother, your son"; "Apostle, behold your mother."
He set forth beforehand the covenant of a bride, teaching by a lofty mystery, lest the sacred childbearing of the virgin should harm the mother's modesty.
To whom Jesus gave assurance by heavenly miracles; the impious crowd did not believe; whoever believed shall be saved.
We believe that God was born, and in the childbearing of the sacred Virgin, who took away the sins of the world, sitting at the right hand of the Father.

div.head: Hymn 4: Veni, redemptor gentium
div.p: Come, Redeemer of the nations, show forth the childbearing of the Virgin; let every age marvel: such a birth befits God.
Not from a man's seed, but by mystic breath, the Word of God was made flesh, and the fruit of the womb blossomed.
The Virgin's womb swells, yet the enclosure of her modesty remains; the banners of virtue gleam, God dwells in the temple.
Coming forth from his chamber, the royal hall of modesty, a giant of twin substance, eager to run his course.
His going forth was from the Father, his return is to the Father; his course extends even to the depths below, his return to the seat of God.
Equal to the eternal Father, gird yourself with the trophy of the flesh, strengthening the weakness of our body with unending power.
Your manger now shines, and the night breathes forth a new light, which no night may interrupt, and may it shine with unbroken faith.

div.head: Hymn 5: Illuminans Altissimus
div.p: The Most High, illuminating the gleaming spheres of the stars, peace, life, light, truth, Jesus, be favourable to those who pray.
Whether by mystic baptism you made the streams of the Jordan once turn back, and are hallowed on this present day for it,
or as a star marked the Virgin's childbirth, gleaming in the sky, and on this same day you led the Magi to worship at the manger,
or into jars full of water you poured in the taste of wine: the servant, well aware, drew out what he himself had not put in.
Seeing the waters take on colour, the streams grow intoxicating; the changed elements are astonished to pass into other uses.
So too, for five thousand men, while you divide five loaves, beneath the teeth of those eating, the food kept growing in their mouths.
It multiplied all the more by its own expenditure of bread: who, seeing this, will not marvel at the unceasing flow of that spring?
Between the hands of those breaking it, the bread flowed abundant: the untouched pieces they had not broken crept in among the men.

div.head: Hymn 6: Orabo mente Dominum
div.p: I shall pray to the Lord with my mind, I shall pray likewise with my spirit; lest the voice alone sing to God, while our understanding, led elsewhere, wanders astray, tossed about, overtaken by empty distractions.

div.head: Hymn 7: Splendor Paternae gloriae
div.p: O Splendour of the Father's glory, bringing forth light from light, O light of the beginnings of the new light, day illuminating day.
And true sun, glide down upon us, gleaming with unending brightness, and pour the radiance of the Holy Spirit into our senses.
With prayers let us also call upon the Father, the Father of everlasting glory, the Father of mighty grace, that he may banish our slippery guilt.
May he shape our vigorous deeds, blunt the teeth of the envious one, give a favourable outcome to harsh mishaps, grant the grace of right conduct.
May he govern and rule our mind, with a chaste and faithful body; may faith glow with warmth, and know nothing of the poisons of deceit.
And may Christ be our food, and may our drink be faith; joyfully let us drink the sober drunkenness of the Spirit.
May this day pass joyfully; let modesty be as the dawn, faith like the noonday, let the mind know no twilight of doubt.
The dawn advances its course; may the whole Dawn come forth, the whole Son in the Father, and the whole Father in the Word.

div.head: Hymn 8: Aeterna Christi munera
div.p: The eternal gifts of Christ, and the victories of the martyrs, offering the praises that are due, let us sing with joyful minds.
The princes of the Churches, the triumphant leaders of the war, soldiers of the heavenly court, and the true lights of the world.
Having conquered the terror of the age, and having scorned the pains of the body, by the shortcut of a sacred death, they possess the blessed life.
The martyrs are handed over to fire, and to the teeth of beasts; the tormentor's insane hand rages, armed with iron claws;
their bared entrails hang exposed, their sacred blood is poured out, but they remain unmoved, through the grace of everlasting life.
The devoted faith of the saints, the unconquered hope of believers, the perfect charity of Christ, triumphs over the prince of the world.
In them is the Father's glory, in them is the will of the Son, in them the Spirit rejoices, heaven is filled with joys.
You now, Redeemer, we beseech, that in fellowship with them you may join your praying servants, unto everlasting ages. Amen.

div.head: Hymn 9: Somno refectis artubus
div.p: With our limbs refreshed by sleep, scorning our bed, we rise; as we sing to you, O Father, we beg you to be present with us.
Let our tongue sing to you first, let the ardour of our mind embrace you; so that of the deeds that follow, you, O holy one, may be the beginning.
Let darkness yield to light, and night to the star of day; so that the guilt which night brought in may crumble away through the gift of light.
We pray likewise as suppliants that you would cut away all our offences, so that you may be praised for ever by the mouths of those who sing to you.
Grant this, most loving Father, and only Son, equal to the Father, together with the Spirit, the Paraclete, reigning through every age.

div.head: Hymn 10: Consors paterni luminis
div.p: Partaker of the Father's light, yourself the light of light, and the day, we break the night by singing; be present to those who entreat you.
Take away the darkness of our minds, put to flight the troops of demons: drive out drowsiness, lest it overwhelm us as we grow slothful.
So, O Christ, grant to all of us who believe your indulgence, that it may profit those who entreat you, what we sing as we chant before dawn.

div.head: Hymn 11: O Lux beata Trinitas
div.p: O blessed Light, O Trinity, and sovereign Unity, already the fiery sun withdraws; pour your light into our hearts.
You, in the morning, with a song of praise, you, in the evening, we beseech; you, our humble glory, let it praise through all ages.

div.head: Hymn 12: Fit porta Christi pervia
div.p: The gate becomes passable for Christ, filled full with grace; and the King passes through, and it remains closed, as it was, throughout the ages.
The offspring of light from on high came forth from the virgin's chamber: bridegroom, redeemer, creator, the giant of his own Church.
The honour and joy of his mother, the boundless hope of believers: through the dark cups of death, he dissolves our sins.
